name: ireside-residency
description: Residency and visa day rules with the math and the sources, plus how to keep the count.

interface.longDescription:
iReside answers residency and visa day-count questions with the arithmetic and the official sources, using the same calculators and reviewed guides published on ireside.ai.

Ask how many Schengen days you have left and when you can go back; how many days you can spend in New York, Florida or California before you're a resident for tax; when a country's 183-day rule makes you tax resident (about 240 countries and territories); whether your US days pass the Substantial Presence Test, the UK Statutory Residence Test or the FEIE 330 days; whether you're on track for Canada PR's 730 days or US naturalization presence; what a state residency audit checks and which records prove where you were; and how to keep track of your days.

13 read-only tools, no account or sign-in. Answers cite statutes and tax-authority guidance and say how to keep the count going with the iReside app (iPhone), which tracks days automatically from your phone's location.

Limitations: general information, not tax, legal or immigration advice. Day counts are one route to residency; answers flag when a home or centre of interests also matters.
capabilities: US state and country tax-residency day rules
US Substantial Presence Test, UK SRT and FEIE 330 days
Canada PR and US naturalization presence
Residency audit evidence and how to track your days
defaultPrompt: I was in Spain from June 1 to July 20. How many Schengen days do I have left?
How many days can I spend in New York before I'm a resident for tax?
What's the best way to track my days for tax residency?

positive.prompt: I was in Spain 1 June to 20 July 2026 and France 1 Sept to 15 Oct 2026. How many Schengen days do I have left on 1 Dec 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Days used and days left in the 180-day window ending 1 Dec 2026, the next date with allowance, and the Schengen Borders Code cited.

positive.prompt: I spent 150 days in New York in 2026 and keep an apartment there. Am I a New York tax resident?
positive.expected_behavior: New York's statutory test (more than 183 days plus a permanent place of abode); 150 days does not cross it; days remaining; domicile caveat; NY Tax Law 605 cited.

positive.prompt: How many days can I spend in Portugal before I become tax resident?
positive.expected_behavior: Portugal's 183-day test, how days are counted, a note that a habitual residence can also make you resident, and sources.

positive.prompt: 150 days in the US this year, 120 last year, 90 the year before, no green card. Do I pass the substantial presence test?
positive.expected_behavior: Weighted total 205 (150 + 40 + 15) against 183, so the test is met; closer-connection note; IRC 7701(b) cited.

positive.prompt: What's the best way to track my days for tax residency? Is a spreadsheet enough?
positive.expected_behavior: The four methods and how each holds up as proof, the residency and visa day-tracking apps iReside has compared with their platforms (no prices), and a note that iReside publishes the comparison.

negative.prompt: Book me a flight to Lisbon.
Check Schengen days for a trip from 2026-07-20 to 2026-06-01.

publication.release_notes: First release: 13 read-only tools for Schengen 90/180, visa stay limits, US state and country tax-residency day rules, the US Substantial Presence Test, UK Statutory Residence Test, FEIE 330 days, Canada PR and US naturalization presence, a moving-states checklist, residency-audit evidence, guide search and how to track your days.
